chapter_theme: Kinds of release and the nirvana of karma (முத்தி பேதம், கரும நிருவாணம்): when release is reached the soul attains Siva without distinction and the primal form becomes its own; those who cling to the one without attachments find him their kin and, gaining his light, fall silent.

2864.reading: When the release spoken of is reached, the soul attains the Supreme, that Siva, without distinction, through turiya; the primal form becoming its own form, faultless nirvana is born.
2864.nuance: உயிர்பர may be உயிர் பரம் (the soul, the Supreme) or உயிர் பர(ம்) எய்தும் (the soul reaches the Supreme). ஆதி சொரூபம் சொரூபத்தது ஆக is taken as the soul taking on the Lord's own nature. நிருவாணம் is both the name of the highest initiation and a word for the freed state; the chapter title (கரும நிருவாணம்) points to the ending of karma.

2865.reading: The supreme being whom those without attachments hold to, the forehead-eyed one whom those without kin regard as kin and who stands around those with no one around them: those who have gained his light and reached him have ceased their babbling.
2865.nuance: The verse plays on பற்று (attachment) and சுற்று (kin, surrounding): having let go of both, the renouncer finds them again in the Lord. பிதற்று (babbling) may be empty talk or the devotee's restless praise; either way, the one who has gained the light falls silent.

links.note: Both make the one without attachment the only thing to cling to: the Kural bids one hold to his hold to let go of holding, Tirumular says the unattached hold to the Supreme and the kinless find him their kin.

In 38 the poet vows never to stop babbling Nandi's name; 2865 says those who gain his light stop babbling. If பிதற்று is the same praise in both, the vow belongs to the seeker and the silence to the one who has arrived.
